# Story 02 — Sign in against the real API and keep the session (Story: CRM-42)

## Prerequisites

-
**IDENTITY-1-API (CRM-41)** shipped `POST /api/v1/sign-in` and `GET /api/v1/me` — see `api/openapi.json
` lines 28–64 and `api/src/features/identity/identity.routes.js` line 12. Coordinate with the API owner only if the froz

en 401 sameness or the 422 `fields` shape needs to change (it must not for this story).
- **LANGUAGES-1
-WEB (CRM-35)** shipped the hardcoded-strings guard at `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`. Every new string added here must be added to **
both** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` in the same commit — `defineLocale` at `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.

ts:6` makes divergence a compile error.
- **PLATFORM-9-WEB** already ships `web/src/app/auth-context.tsx`, `web/src/sh

ared/api/client.ts`, `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts`, and `web/src/testing/render.tsx`. **Use them; do not reimplement.**
- Read `.squad/plan-l
essons.md` end to end before starting. L-15 (run `npm run build`, not only the suite) and L-16 (prove the guard fails on a regression) are load

-bearing here.

---

## Story Goal

The sign-in screen calls the real API, stores the token the API issues, and takes the visitor to `/`
. A refusal shows the API's `code` verbatim (no sentence written into the screen), clears the password field, and leaves the email in place. The submit button is dis
abled while the request is in flight, and the loading state comes from `useRequest`, not from a local boolean. A reload keeps the session (already true through `AuthPro

vider`; this story preserves the seam).

Explicitly **not in scope**: expired-token handling mid-session (IDENTITY-3-
WEB), account management (IDENTITY-2-WEB), password change (IDENTITY-6/7-WEB), the desk shell (PLATFORM-12-WEB), the empty/loading/error design system (PLATFORM

-16-WEB), and **any** API change. If the API surface looks short, note it and stop — do not add routes here.

---

## Context — Read These Files First

1
. `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx` (whole file, 57 lines) — the current screen. Line 21 writes `signIn('stub-token')`; that line, the
two `IDENTITY-1-API` comments at lines 19–20, and the `stubNotice` text at line 52 are what this story deletes and replaces. Note the prim

itives already used (`Card`, `Field`, `Heading`, `Stack`, `Text`, `Button`).
2. `web/src/app/auth-context.tsx` (whole file, 75 lines) — do
**not** change the shape. `signIn(token: string)` at line 37 is the seam; the token you pass here is what `localStorage` receives at
line 39 and what the HTTP client will read via `setAuthTokenGetter` at line 58. Comments at lines 6–9 explicitly call the current

token "STUB"; those comments must be updated (or removed) so the file no longer describes a stub.
3. `web/src/shared/api/client.ts` (56 lines) — use
`request<T>(path, init)`. It prefixes `/api/v1` via `API_BASE_URL` (line 1) and attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when
the getter returns one (lines 22–23). A network failure throws `ApiError({ status: 0, code: 'INTERNAL', requestId: null })` (line

31). 4xx/5xx bodies are parsed into `ApiError` with `code`, `status`, `requestId`, and `fields` (lines 50–55). `path` must start with `/` (line 14).
4. `web/src
/shared/api/errors.ts` (39 lines) — `ApiErrorCode` includes `UNAUTHENTICATED`, `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `INTERNAL`. The class car

ries `code`, `status`, `requestId`, `fields?`.
5. `web/src/shared/hooks/useRequest.ts` (44 lines) — the ONLY place a screen expresses loading (com
ment lines 5–6). `run(task)` sets `status: 'loading'`, returns/throws through the task, and the monotonic `lat
est.current` ticket (line 15) drops stale answers. `status`, `data`, `error`, `run` are the return shape (

line 43).
6. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` lines 5–17 and `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` lines 6–18 — the current `signIn`
block. Keys must be added to both. `defineLocale` (en.ts lines 34–43) rejects a key in one file that the other lacks and r

ejects extras — so both files change or neither compiles.
7. `web/src/testing/render.tsx` (47 lines) — `renderWithProviders(ui, { route, language
, signedIn })`. Line 28 shows `signedIn: true` writes the literal `'stub-token'`; `signedIn: '<real-token>'` writes a ca
ller-supplied token. Providers nest **router → i18n → auth**. Tests that need a `fetch` response use `vi.stubGlobal('

fetch', …)`; the default `fetch` throws when unstubbed (see `web/src/testing/setup.ts`).
8. `web/src/app/routing.test.tsx` (46 lines) — the test at line 23 clicks "Sign in"
and asserts `localStorage.getItem(AUTH_TOKEN_KEY)` is `'stub-token'` (line 29). This assertion must change once the button issues a real request; either st
ub `fetch` in that test or move that assertion into the sign-in page tests and replace it with an assertion that only cares about "signed in ⇒ desk he

ading".
9. `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` lines 30, 96–107 — the AST walk that fails the build if a
new string lands in `pages/` without going through `t`. Any new label (error banner, "signing in…") must live

in `en.ts` and `ar.ts`.
10. `api/openapi.json` lines 28–64 — the contract this screen calls. 200 body: `{ token, user: { id, role, name } }`.

401 body is deliberately identical for wrong password / unknown address / disabled account. 422 body carries `fields`.
11. `api/src/
features/identity/identity.test.js` lines 25, 88, 101, 119 — the request/response shapes the API actually returns; use as

reference when writing test fixtures for `fetch` stubs.
12. `scripts/criteria/identity.md`, section **## IDENTITY-1

-WEB** — the four acceptance criteria this story is judged against. Reproduced verbatim in the intake.

- Grep to prove the stub is gone after
the change: search `web/` for `stub-token`. Only `web/src/testing/render.tsx:28` (test helper default) and (opt
ionally) `web/src/shared/api/client.test.ts` may retain it; `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx` and `web/src/app/routing.test.tsx` must no longer contain it.
- Grep to prove no page invented an English sentence: `git diff` under `web/src/pages/` must not add

any string literal captured by the guard at `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.

---

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current beha
viour:** submit writes the literal `'stub-token'` into the auth context and navigates to `/`; no network call happ

ens; the password stays in the field; there is no loading state; the screen shows a `stubNotice` explaining it is not real.
- **New behaviour:**

- Submit calls `POST /api/v1/sign-in` with `{ email, password }` via `request()`.
  - On 200, pass the returned `token` (**

not** any local fabrication) to `signIn(token)`, then `navigate('/', { replace: true })`.
  - On any error, keep the email,

**clear the password** (`setPassword('')`), and show the API's `code` verbatim (see string rules below).
  - The submit button is `disabled` when

`status === 'loading'`; the loading state comes from `useRequest`, never from a local `useState<boolean>`.
  - Nothing outside `web/src/testing/render.tsx` may write `'stub-token'`.

**
String rules — no sentences in the screen.** The screen renders `t.signIn.errors[error.code]` (or a `t.signIn.errors.default` fallback) so
translations live entirely in the resource files, in both languages, per the intake's explicit instruction. The screen source cont

ains no `"Wrong email or password"`-style prose.

---

## Frontend Tasks

_No backend changes required._ The API
this screen calls is already shipped by CRM-41 (`api/openapi.json` lines 28–64, `api/src/features/identity/identity.routes.js:12`). If a g

ap is discovered while implementing, stop and raise it; do not extend the API in this story.

### 1 — Rewrite `SignInPage` to call the API

**File:

    event.preventDefault();
    try {
      const { token } = await run(() =>
        request<SignInResponse>('/sign-in', {
          method: 'POST',
          body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
        }),

Do not** introduce a `useState<boolean>` for loading. The button's `disabled` is derived from `status` (or `status === 'loading'`).
- **Do not** translate `error.code` inline in J

SX — read it out of `t.signIn.errors`.
- Keep the primitive assembly (`Card`, `Field`, `Heading`, `Stack`, `Button`,

`Text`); do not add new CSS, spacing or radii — see the comment already at `SignInPage.tsx` lines 8–9.
- Path passed to `request()` is `

/sign-in` (client prefixes `/api/v1`; see `web/src/shared/api/client.ts:1`).
- Keep `autoComplete="username"`
and `autoComplete="current-password"` on the fields (already at lines 36, 46). Do not alter `id`, `name`, `type` attributes —

the guard at `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts:34–43` deliberately does not flag them.

### 2 — Add error

and disabled-state strings to both locales

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` (extend the `signIn` block starting line 6
Wording is provisional; the point is that **the screen names an error code and reads a message from here

**.
- Optional: `submitting: 'Signing in…'` if the button label changes while loading. If added, both files get

it.

**File:** `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` (mirror the change in the `signIn` block starting line 7).

- Because `defineLocale` (en.ts l

- Remove `stubNotice` here

too (line 12).

### 3 — Cleanse `AuthProvider` of stub-era commentary

**File:** `web/src/app/auth-context.tsx` lines 6–9

and the inline "the reload will not remember it" line at 41.

- Rewrite the header comment: the token st
ored here is now what the API issued, so lines 6–9 must no longer say "STUB … any non-empty string counts as a session". Say

plainly: "The token stored here is what the API issued; `AuthProvider` reads it synchronously on first render so a reload keeps the session."
- **Do not** change any exported sym
bol or its signature. `signIn(token: string)`, `signOut()`, `isAuthenticated`, `AUTH_TOKEN_KEY` stay exactly as they
are. The auth-context tests (via `renderWithProviders`) and `web/src/shared/api/client.ts:22` all read this

shape.

### 4 — Update the routing tests that assert the stub token

**File:** `web/src/app/routing.test.tsx` lines 23–34.

- The test titled "signing in re
aches the desk, and signing out returns to sign-in" clicks the sign-in button and asserts `localStorage.getItem(AUTH_TOKEN_KEY

)).toBe('stub-token')` (line 29). After the change, the button issues a real request; that assertion must:
  - Either stub `fetch` for this test with
`vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(new Response(JSON.stringify({ token: 'server-token', user: {…} }), { status: 200, headers: {

'content-type': 'application/json' } })))` and assert `…).toBe('server-token')`;
  - Or move the "reaches the desk" and "signs out" ass
ertions to a new sign-in-page test file (task 5) and simplify the routing test to signed-in-vs-not,

keeping `localStorage` unstubbed.
- Keep the other four tests as-is (they use `renderWithProviders({ signedIn: true })` which contin

ues to work through the test helper's default `'stub-token'`).

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **401 UNAUTHENTICATED** — wrong password, unknown email, dis
abled account. The API answers them identically on purpose (`api/openapi.json:39`). The screen must not attempt to distinguish; it renders `t.signIn.errors.UNAUTHENTICATED

` and clears the password field.
- **422 VALIDATION_FAILED** — well-formed JSON but wrong shape (empty email/password). Body carries `fields` names (`api/openapi.json:42
`). The screen renders `t.signIn.errors.VALIDATION_FAILED`; do **not** render field values. `error.fields` may be logged/inspected but nothing values

-related is rendered.
- **Network failure or `fetch` reject** — `request()` throws `ApiError({ status: 0, code: 'INTERNAL', … })

` (client.ts:31). `useRequest` funnels non-`ApiError` throws into the same code (useRequest.ts:31–34). The screen renders `t.signIn.errors.INTERNAL`.
- **
Unknown/new API code** — the API's frozen catalogue is at `web/src/shared/api/errors.ts:5–13`,
but the wire may still return something the screen has not mapped. Use `t.signIn.errors[error.code] ?? t.signIn.errors.default` so the screen

never renders `undefined`.
- **Double-submit** — the second click while `status === 'loading'` must not fire a second request. Enforced by the `disab
led` on the button; belt-and-braces, the `latest` ticket in `useRequest` drops stale answers if it happens through another

path.
- **Storage blocked / private window** — `signIn()` swallows the write failure (auth-context.tsx:38

–42); the tab remains signed in, a reload does not. Unchanged behaviour; do not regress it.
- **Reload with a stored token** — `
readStoredToken()` runs synchronously in `useState(readStoredToken)` (auth-context.tsx:35). This is what mak

es a reload keep the session. Nothing in this story may replace it with a `useEffect`.
- **RTL language** — `renderWithProviders({ language: 'ar' })` contin
ues to render Arabic labels (`routing.test.tsx:41–45`). Error strings added in Arabic must render RTL without

extra work; verify with the test in task 5.

---

## Test Plan

1. **New: `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.test.ts
x`** — unit-level tests using `renderWithProviders` and `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', …)`. Mirror the fetch stubbing pattern from other web tests;

   - "submits email and password to
`/api/v1/sign-in` and stores the API's token" — assert the `fetch` call URL/method/body, then `localStorage.getItem(AUTH_TOKEN_KEY

the mock with a valid response, expect `screen.findByRole('heading', { name: 'Support Desk' })`.
   - "on 401, renders `t.signIn.errors.UNAUT
HENTICATED`, clears the password, keeps the email, and leaves the submit button enabled again" — resolve the mock with a `Response` of status 401 body `{ code: 'UNAUT

HENTICATED', requestId: 'req_x' }`.
   - "on 422, renders `t.signIn.errors.VALIDATION_FAILED` and never a subm

itted value" — mock a 422 response with `fields: ['email']`; assert the email string typed is not present in the rendered error.
   - "on network failure, ren

ders `t.signIn.errors.INTERNAL`" — mock `fetch` to reject; verify the shape of `ApiError` funnelling.
   - "the submit button is disabled while the

request is in flight" — resolve the mock via a deferred promise; assert `getByRole('button', { name: t.signIn.submit }).disabled` before and after.
   - "renders in Arabic through `renderWithProviders({ language: 'ar' })

`" — smoke.
2. **Update: `web/src/app/routing.test.tsx`** — either stub `fetch` for the "signing in reaches the desk" test (line 23–34) and assert the server
-issued token, or replace that assertion with a heading assertion and move token specifics to the new sign-in test file. The reload-surv

ives-a-reload test (line 17) must remain green unchanged.
3. **Update (light): `web/src/shared/i18n` snapshot in
`web/src/shared/ui/primitives.test.tsx`** — the file compares `ar.signIn.heading !== en.signIn.heading` (line 74). If any

new key breaks that specific test, adjust it in kind; do not weaken it.
4. **Regression: `web/src/pages/no
-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`** — must stay green. To satisfy L-16, temporarily add a literal like `<Text>Wrong email or password</Text>` in

`SignInPage.tsx`, run the suite, confirm the guard fails with the exact line/column, then revert.
5. **Regression: `web

/src/shared/api/client.test.ts`** — 33 web tests must still pass. Do not touch this file unless task 4 requires it.

---

## Migration / Rollback

- No schema or config changes. The only user-visible change is that

the sign-in button now actually calls the API and can fail.
- **Rollback:** revert the three files (`SignInPage.tsx`, `en.ts`, `ar.
ts`) and the routing-test edit. The auth-context comment change is cosmetic and safe either way. There is no half
-applied state to worry about because nothing persists across the boundary except the token in `localStorage`, which is opaque to the schema.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend builds:** in `web/`, run `npm run build`. Must succeed — this is L-15

. `tsc` is what proves the ar/en `defineLocale` change was mirrored.
2. **Frontend runs tests:** in `web/`, run `npm test`. All

33 pre-existing tests plus the new sign-in tests must pass. Zero snapshot updates.
3. **Backend regression:** in `api/`, run `npm test`. All

102 tests must still pass (this story does not touch the API, but confirm nothing here demanded a fixture change).
4. **
Stub-token audit:** from repo root, run `grep -rn "stub-token" web/`. Expected matches: `web/src/test
ing/render.tsx:28` and (if unchanged) `web/src/shared/api/client.test.ts:77,82`. **No match may appear in `web/src/pages/**`

or `web/src/app/**` (except the test helper).**
5. **Hardcoded-strings guard:** confirm task 4 in Test Plan was performed and

reverted; the guard fails on a literal in `pages/`, then the suite goes green again after revert.
6. **AI att
ribution audit:** from repo root, run `grep -rniE "ai[- ]?generated|copilot|chatgpt|assistant" -

- .` on the diff. Zero matches in code, docs, ignore files, or commit messages.
7. **Manual smoke (
optional but recommended):** in `web/`, run `npm run dev`; sign in with a seeded admin (see `api/src/plat
form/db/seed.js`); observe the request in DevTools, the token in `localStorage['support-desk.auth-token']`, and the reload beh

aviour. Sign out returns to `/sign-in`.

---
